- Proven technical expertise across geology, reservoir engineering, drilling, hydraulic fracturing, gas processing and production optimisation

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Exploration and geological risk — Inherent geological and exploration uncertainty affects reserve and production estimates; mitigated through geological studies, seismic interpretation, reservoir modelling, technical peer review and phased investment decisions.
- Project execution risk — Delays in drilling, hydrofracturing, approvals and infrastructure completion (e.g. GGS-1/GGS-2, evacuation pipelines) can defer commercial production; addressed through detailed project planning, experienced project management and milestone review.
- Commodity price risk — Volatility in international crude oil, natural gas and LNG prices affects project economics; management monitors market developments and focuses on operational efficiency for resilience.
- Regulatory risk — Evolving regulatory, environmental and taxation frameworks, and dependence on approvals such as Right of Way / Right of Use, affect project timelines; managed through regular engagement with regulatory authorities.
- Financial risk (liquidity, credit, interest rate, forex) — The Company is exposed to liquidity, credit, interest rate and foreign exchange risk, managed through prudent financial policies and efficient capital structure management.
- Health, safety and environmental risk — Drilling and production operations carry inherent HSE risk; managed through comprehensive HSE systems, preventive maintenance, training and emergency preparedness.
- Import dependence and macro exposure — High import dependence exposes India (and by extension the sector) to supply disruptions and foreign exchange volatility, alongside geopolitical uncertainty and cost inflation in steel, drilling services, equipment, logistics and skilled manpower.
- Early-stage / concentrated asset-development risk — Financial performance currently reflects continued investment in long-gestation CBM/exploration projects (North Karanpura, Jharia) with revenue from producing assets still limited relative to the scale of the asset base; profitability depends on timely commissioning of a small number of key assets.

It sells natural gas to business-to-business customers -- public sector undertakings, gas marketing/trading companies and industrial/commercial consumers -- with connectivity to the national gas grid, and operates in a single reportable business segment (exploration and production of oil and gas).

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Accelerating Commercialisation of Existing Assets: foremost priority is timely monetisation of existing assets, emphasising accelerated production from North Karanpura and Jharia CBM blocks while optimising output from the Rajasthan marginal gas fields.
- Expanding the Reserve Base: continued investment in exploration -- geological/geophysical data acquisition, exploratory drilling and reservoir evaluation -- together with evaluation of new acreage and discovered small fields to support long-term reserve replacement.
- Strengthening Leadership in Coal Bed Methane: leverage CBM expertise to improve well productivity, enhance recovery factors and expedite commercial production through timely completion of surface infrastructure.
- Operational Excellence and Cost Optimisation: optimise drilling programmes and well design, improve reservoir management and production surveillance, enhance preventive maintenance and procurement, and continuously monitor capital and operating expenditure.
- Technology and Digital Transformation: advanced geological and reservoir modelling, AI and data analytics for field optimisation, digital production monitoring and predictive maintenance.
- Financial Discipline and ESG: investment decisions guided by rigorous technical and commercial evaluation, controlled leverage and efficient working capital management, alongside strategic priorities around emissions reduction, energy efficiency, water management and corporate governance.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Capex/expansion activity is concentrated in commissioning the two CBM blocks: at North Karanpura CBM (Hazaribagh & Chatra, Jharkhand), GGS-1 and GGS-2 construction is in progress along with interconnecting evacuation pipelines, and IOCL is separately laying a ~68 km gas evacuation pipeline from the block to the Urja Ganga Pipeline, expected to be commissioned soon. At Jharia CBM Block-I (Damodar Valley, Jharkhand), de-watering pump installation is to be completed in August 2026, PNGRB has authorised a ~9 km pipeline connecting the block to the Urja Ganga pipeline, and infield pipelines plus an Early Production System (EPS) are being set up to position the company for imminent first gas sales, alongside continuing Phase-1 development drilling (5 of a planned set of wells drilled to date). At the Rajasthan Marginal Gas Fields (Jaisalmer), a Gas Gathering Station was built at Bankia in 2012 with separation, purification, dehydration and compression facilities and ~15 km of connecting pipeline; no further expansion project is described there beyond ongoing efforts to sell the gas.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising urbanisation, an expanding manufacturing base, growing transportation demand and increasing per capita energy consumption continue to drive sustained demand for hydrocarbons even as renewable capacity expands.
- India remains one of the world's largest consumers and importers of crude oil and petroleum products, with domestic production facing structural challenges from natural decline of mature fields, rising water cut and complexity of frontier basins -- keeping enhanced domestic E&P a strategic national priority.
- Government policy support via HELP, OALP and CBM licensing/bidding reforms, with marketing and pricing freedom, is expected to unlock India's unconventional gas resources and favour companies with strong technical and execution capability.
- Natural gas is assuming a growing role in India's transition to a lower-carbon economy, supporting investment across exploration, gathering, compression, processing, transmission and LNG/city-gas distribution infrastructure; mandatory CBG blending and ethanol blending progress reflect broader energy diversification.
- Sector headwinds include volatility in international crude oil/LNG prices, geopolitical uncertainty, forex fluctuations, cost inflation, Right of Way/Right of Use approval delays and increasing environmental compliance requirements.
- With gas sales from North Karanpura CBM having commenced and Jharia CBM progressing towards first gas sales, management expects commissioning of these assets to improve operating leverage, revenues and profitability over the medium term.
- The long-term outlook for India's upstream industry is viewed as positive, favouring companies with proven technical expertise, disciplined execution and prudent capital allocation.
- Gas sales contract signed for 20,000 SCMD at the North Karanpura CBM Block; gas sales commenced April 2025.
